reason: Paper 2 backs its main claims with a large controlled study: 11 optimizers, about 2900 runs, tuning matched across model size, batch size and training horizon. That study yields concrete, checkable findings, such as AdEMAMix/MARS leading at scale, the weight-decay fix that makes D-Muon work, and codebase defaults (z-loss, 10% LR decay) that flip optimizer rankings, though it stops at 720M parameters and uses single seeds. Paper 1 offers a useful, timely and harder benchmark. However, its evidence is thin: one scaffold, single Pass@1 runs, a weak GPL-based contamination argument, a commercial set no one can audit, and numbers that disagree between text and tables (Sonnet 16.3 vs 17.6, GPT-4o 3.9 vs 4.9, failure-mode percentages). Its analysis adds little insight beyond the dataset itself.
recognized: Paper 1 appears to be SWE-Bench Pro (Scale AI, 2025)
Paper 2 appears to be 'Benchmarking Optimizers for Large Language Model Pretraining' (EPFL, 2025)
